reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Declaration of marriage public policy
headings.reviewNote: Archived statutory text declaring state public policy to recognize marriage only between a man and a woman.

headings.title: Invalidity of marriages not between man and woman
headings.reviewNote: Archived statutory text stating that any purported marriage not between a man and a woman is invalid.

headings.title: Restriction on recorder license issuance
headings.reviewNote: Archived statutory text stating that no recorder shall issue a marriage license except to a man and a woman.

headings.title: Nonrecognition of same-sex marriages from other jurisdictions
headings.reviewNote: Archived statutory text stating that a marriage between persons of the same sex will not be recognized for any purpose in Missouri even when valid where contracted.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 1996 S.B. 768 § 6, A.L. 2001 H.B. 157) and source case annotations (St. Louis Health Care Network v. State, 1998; Lawson v. Kelly, 2014; Obergefell v. Hodges, 2014); maintained strictly neutral archived-text framing without enforceability claims.

headings.title: Mandatory marriage license and authorized solemnization
headings.reviewNote: Requires obtaining a marriage license beforehand and solemnization by an authorized person for a marriage contracted in Missouri to be recognized as valid.

headings.title: License application in presence or military and incarcerated exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires signing a marriage license application before the recorder/deputy or electronically online, and provides affidavit, SSN, and photo-ID procedures for incarcerated or out-of-state/country active-duty military applicants.

headings.title: Social Security number requirement and 30-day expiration
headings.reviewNote: Requires each applicant's Social Security number (exempt from copying under section 610.024) or non-issuance statement, directs license issuance unless withdrawn, and voids the license thirty days after issuance.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of this section as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Invalidation of common-law marriages
headings.reviewNote: Declares common-law marriages null and void.

headings.title: Validity preserved against official authority defects
headings.reviewNote: Preserves validity of a marriage despite lack of authority in the person solemnizing under section 451.100 if consummated with full belief by either party that they were lawfully joined.

headings.title: Online application identity verification and residency limit
headings.reviewNote: Requires recorders using an online process without in-person verification to use two-step or independent identity verification for both applicants and restricts online applications/issuance to cases where at least one applicant resides in the county or independent city.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (through A.L. 2025 H.B. 737 & 486 merged with S.B. 43) and 2014 Amos v. Higgins annotation; replaced incorrect subsection 7 heading (drafted as nonresident waiting-period preemption) with online-application identity verification and county-residency rules.

headings.title: Recorder duty to issue license and statutory form
headings.reviewNote: Directs county recorders and the City of St. Louis recorder to issue a marriage license to any legally entitled applicant and sets out the permissive statutory marriage license form.

headings.title: Fifteen-day return and solemnization certificate form
headings.reviewNote: Requires the person solemnizing the marriage to make a return within fifteen days after issuance using the prescribed certificate form and return the license to the issuing officer.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text including both embedded form tables (through A.L. 2025 H.B. 737 & 486 merged with S.B. 43); updated subsections 1 and 2 titles to separate the license form in subsection 1 from the 15-day solemnization return form in subsection 2.

headings.title: Prohibition on marriage licenses for persons under eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any recorder from issuing a marriage license authorizing the marriage of any male or female under eighteen years of age.

headings.title: Proof of age documentation required
headings.reviewNote: Requires the recorder to state in every license whether applicants are of age and requires applicants to present a certified birth certificate, passport, or other government-issued ID for documentation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (A.L. 2025 H.B. 737 & 486 merged with S.B. 43); replaced outdated subsection 1 heading and note that referenced repealed parental-consent exceptions, reflecting the absolute prohibition for persons under age eighteen.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for recorder refusal or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Makes a recorder's willful neglect or refusal to issue a license upon section 451.150 fee tender, or failure to record the license and return (archived text: 'fail to refuse to record'), a misdemeanor punishable by a $5 to $100 fine.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for failure or false return
headings.reviewNote: Makes failure to return a license within fifteen days, making a false return, or a recorder willfully making a false record a misdemeanor punishable under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (RSMo 1939 § 3367, A.L. 2001 H.B. 157); retained both drafted titles and noted the archived text phrasing 'fail to refuse to record' in subsection 1.

headings.title: Additional twenty-dollar marriage license fee
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an additional $20 marriage license fee paid by the applicant and collected by the recorder of deeds upon issuance.

headings.title: Additional seven-dollar fee for certified copies
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an additional $7 fee for a certified copy of a marriage license and authorizes the recorder to distinguish certified copies from photocopies.

headings.title: Monthly fee distribution to trust funds
headings.reviewNote: Directs the recorder monthly to forward $15 per license and $7 per certified copy to the section 210.173 children's trust fund and pay $5 per license to the county treasurer for a domestic violence shelter special trust fund under sections 455.200 to 455.230.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 1990 H.B. 1370 § 9, A.L. 1992 H.B. 894); retained all three drafted titles and verified fee amounts ($20 license, $7 certified copy) and monthly allocations to section 210.173 and sections 455.200 to 455.230 funds.

headings.title: Separate property rights of married spouses
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that premarital and coverture-acquired real and personal property, wages, personal-rights claims, and income remain a spouse's separate property under sole control and exempt from the other spouse's debts.

headings.title: Possession with assent, necessaries liability, and legal actions
headings.reviewNote: Requires written express assent to reduce separate personal property to a spouse's possession, subjects such property to specified spousal and family-necessaries debts, and authorizes independent suits and cost execution (original-rolls footnote: 'a').

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (RSMo 1939 § 3390, A.L. 2001 H.B. 537), original-rolls footnote ('a'), and 1954-1955 case annotations (Herbert v. Herbert; Hamilton v. Fulkerson); retained both drafted titles.
